r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: TheComparisonHasTeeth is NOT passing incidentally - probed three ways, all confirming. T1 neuter the encoder poison to a no-op -> test_an_environment_dependent_encoder_is_caught goes RED, so the poison and not the harness is what makes the bytes differ. T2 neuter the varying-field poison -> test_a_varying_field_placed_outside_run_is_caught goes RED. T3 poison the CONTROL path -> test_the_real_producer_is_byte_identical_through_this_harness goes RED, so the control genuinely runs the unpoisoned producer. The harness therefore discriminates in both directions. THE NON-OBVIOUS RESULT of my own mutation set: D4 - the envelope growing a varying key that is NOT added to CONTENT_KEYS - is caught ONLY by the bidirectional set assertion, never by the byte comparison, because the allow-list correctly drops the key from content before the bytes are compared. So the allow-list and the bidirectional assertion are COMPLEMENTARY, not redundant: the allow-list is what makes a new key non-content by default, and bidirectionality is the only thing that can see the key exists at all. Either alone leaves a hole. Deny-to-admit dropped nothing legitimate: over the real Commander manifest and 9 real gated templates, old deny-spelling and new admit-spelling give identical keys, identical ORDER (CONTENT_KEYS order == envelope order, which matters because json.dumps preserves dict order), and byte-identical encodings - 0 differences. RealCheckoutSkew is genuinely non-vacuous now: baseline green, and neutering its tracked rows to absent paths (reproducing the exact old all-null vacuity) turns it RED. Producer behaviour is unchanged from rework 1 across my 16 adversarial declarations.
